quest.title: Middle Note: Blood Due
quest.description: The disputes behind "Auguste" seem to be far more complex than you expected...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x650, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: Pomum de Ambra Chapter: Act I
chapter.title: Floral Debt, Blood Due

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Emilie is doing her best to treat her Master... We shouldn't interrupt her.)

talks.objective: Head to the vicinity of the hotel

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Emilie!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's Edgar?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: No longer in critical condition, thankfully. He's still very weak, but with a bit more rest, he should regain consciousness soon.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: My chemical analysis of "Auguste" also went smoothly, although it certainly raised some questions...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Questions...?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Mhm... I was able to identify the components that give the substance its fragrance... but I also noticed an abnormal trace of elemental energy in the sample.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Elemental energy!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would that have an effect on the body?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Hard to say. It was such a minute amount, proportionally speaking... like mixing a single drop of perfume into the ocean...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: I had to use one of the newest tests developed in recent years to even detect the traces present in the sample.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Unless you were abnormally sensitive to elemental energy, I doubt it would have any effect, even if you used the product every day for ten years.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: As for whether Master's condition was caused by the elemental energy present in the sample or some other component of the perfume... It's still too early to say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That reminds Paimon, did Tighnari come and find you? Maybe we could ask him to take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Hm, I received a message from him last night, but I haven't heard anything since. The message said he was looking into some information at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon thought he might've stopped by to see you first...
Um, excuse me... Is Miss Emilie here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Collei?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #Oh, perfect! Familiar faces! {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you're here too!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Collei... Ah, of course, Tighnari's apprentice! He's mentioned you many times. It's a pleasure to finally meet you!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: And, please... No need for formalities. Emilie is just fine.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... O—Okay! Nice to meet you too, Mi— *ahem* Emilie.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did Tighnari send you here, Collei?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yep... Master and the others went through decades' worth of records last night, and still haven't had a chance to rest... I'm fast on my feet, so it only made sense for me to come and give you an update.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Anyway, based on what they've reviewed so far, they believe there's no indication that a researcher by the name of "Vijava" ever passed through the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could it have been an alias?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Master considered that possibility as well... But, the name wasn't the only dead end. Master tried to track down people with a similar research direction or background, but also couldn't find a match.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How is that possible...

choices.text: Maybe her identity as a researcher from Sumeru...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: It's starting to seem very likely. If we want to figure out her true identity, I'm afraid another conversation with those two merchants might be our only...

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Hey...!

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Lucien...!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That voice! It's...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's Sylvain! Wait, you don't think Kirya came back, do you?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: That seems impossible... If someone came in or out of the hotel just now, we would've seen them...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go inside and check!

choices.text: Was a ruse all along.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You rush into the hallway and head for Lucien's room. You try to enter, but the door won't budge...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It's locked?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll try to break it open.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You rush into the hallway and head for Sylvain's room. You try to enter, but the door won't budge...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It's locked?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll try to break it open.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Aw...

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: ...Lucien! Lucien! Come on, wake up!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is he going to be okay?

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: Emilie... Emilie! My brother... He's gonna be okay, right? He's just unconscious... like what happened to Edgar?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry, Mr. Sylvain, but... we were too late this time.

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: No... No... That's not... That's not possible...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}, Collei, Mr. Sylvain has gone through a huge shock...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: He needs some space to calm down. Could one of you take him next door? It's not good for him to look at his brother's body like this.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...Of course. Leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll notify the sheriff.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Thank you both.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Mr. Sylvain, let's get you up. Here, take my hand. Nice and slow.

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: A—Ah... Ah...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: We'll take things from here. Just focus on getting some rest... Here, this way...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Poor guy... He's like a shell of his former self...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He may have made some bad decisions in life, but... Right now, Paimon can't help but feel sorry for him.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Good person or bad... The death of a loved one is equally painful.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: All the moments he shared with his brother, every hardship and triumph they endured together... are now memories he has to carry alone.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe that's what Kirya wanted...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Kirya really was behind this, then what exactly did he do to Lucien...?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Lucien can no longer speak, but the traces left behind by his death most certainly can.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, I've got things covered here at the scene. I'll leave you to contact the sheriff.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Some time passes, and Sheriff Shyam rushes to the scene...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Who would've thought... Yesterday's case is still up in the air, and now this happens...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Miss Emilie, I heard you're an experienced forensic doctor. Have you been able to discover anything?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Oh, I'm not actually a forensic doctor. I just happen to have some relevant knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: I did take a look, though... Judging by the temperature and rigidity of the body, it appears the time of death was sometime last night. I'd have to do a more thorough investigation to find out more.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Then... would you mind helping us investigate? Before he left, Tighnari said we could trust your judgment if something like this were to happen.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Of course. I appreciate your trust. Many of the traces left behind at the scene will fade with time, so the sooner we investigate the better.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll help too! We don't know much about dead bodies... But, you can leave the other clues to us!

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: (This door leads to the hallway. The lock is intact, and there are no signs of damage.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This door was probably locked last night...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And the windows are shut tight too... Seems like the only way to get in would've been through Sylvain's room...

dialogues.speaker: Incense
dialogues.text: (The incense slowly rising into the air... It seems familiar somehow.)

dialogues.speaker: Flowers
dialogues.text: (The corners are filled with flowers from different nations. The fragrance is incredibly strong.)

dialogues.speaker: Luggage
dialogues.text: (This bag is stuffed with clothes and other daily necessities. It's quite heavy.)

dialogues.speaker: Cabinet
dialogues.text: (The space inside the cabinet is divided into various compartments... It doesn't look like a person could hide in there.)

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Pupils are dilated, skin is flushed... No overt external injuries or signs of a struggle...

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: (This door leads to Sylvain's room. I can hear faint voices coming from the other side...)

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: Lucien... Why...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry for your loss...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Sylvain still needs more time to calm down. We should finish investigating Lucien's room first...)

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: So, did you find anything?

choices.text: There are no signs of forced entry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can show you... Here, it'd be something like this!

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: But... Entering through the room next door without alerting Sylvain... Wait, you don't think Sylvain could've been the one who...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...No, his reaction to the loss of his brother seemed genuine, and he doesn't have a motive.

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: Then, what could've happened last night... I know Sylvain is still in shock, but he's our only available witness. We have to take his statement.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: I agree. Also, I've made some new discoveries, so we might as well head next door and go through everything together.

choices.text: The only way in would've been through Sylvain's room.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You enter Sylvain's room. He looks much calmer...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: ...Mr. Sylvain, I need you to tell me everything you and your brother did since yesterday afternoon. Did you see or hear anything strange?

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: ...After Kirya attacked Edgar, my brother and I were incredibly careful...

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: We returned to our rooms and decided to lock all the doors leading to the hallway.

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: The only door we kept unlocked was the one connecting our rooms. That way, if we heard any commotion coming from the other room, we could help each other...

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: ...But, I didn't hear any sort of commotion last night! Not a single noise! I woke up this morning, opened the door, and Lucien... Lucien was...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: ...So, no movement from the room next door, no forced entry via Sylvain's room...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: No signs of a struggle at the scene, and no external injuries on Lucien's body... What kind of cause of death are we dealing with here?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: I did notice a few things about the body: Lucien's pupils were dilated and his skin was flushed... Very similar to Master's symptoms after the attack yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: There weren't any traces of liquid in his mouth or nose, so it's unlikely he was forced to ingest anything... The more plausible explanation is that he inhaled a substance without knowing it... and I'd say that substance was likely "Auguste."

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: "Auguste"...? No, that's not possible... Inhaling "Auguste" won't kill you! And, anyway, it would have been for just one night!

choices.text: "Just one night"?

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: N—No... that's not what I meant...!

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Emilie! You ran your tests, didn't you? Go on, tell everyone whether you found any poison!

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...No, I didn't find any common toxins.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Hah... See? "Auguste" is harmless... The market response proved that years ago!

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: ...That may be true for most people, but not for everyone.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Master...!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Edgar! You're up and about already?

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: ...*cough*! Thanks to Emilie, I'm out of the woods for now.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: ...Sylvain, no matter how hard you may try to hide it, the truth will always come to light.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Edgar...!

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: Even if we could keep it a secret for another ten or twenty years... Do you think Kirya would just let us be?

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: No... He would never give up... not if he's doing all of this for Yelena.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yelena...?

choices.text: So, you're saying prolonged exposure is dangerous?

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: That's "Vijava's" real name.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: ...Yelena wasn't a scholar from Sumeru. She was an exiled Fatuus from Snezhnaya.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...A Fatuus!?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: The Fatui... That means, the elemental energy present in "Auguste" was...!

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Ah, so you already detected it... Well, Sylvain, looks like there's truly no reason to hide things now.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: The Auguste flower... was created with the mutative and distorting power of a Delusion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—A Delusion!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: The Fatui, Delusions... I never would've thought "Auguste" was hiding this many secrets...

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Born of a Delusion, "Auguste" contained distorted elemental energy... Prolonged exposure over many years could have a harmful effect on the body... *coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: ...That's enough, Edgar. I'll take it from here.

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: At first, Yelena wanted to keep refining the perfume and the flower, but no one knew how long the "Perfume Mania" was going to last back then.

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: It didn't have an effect on ordinary people, anyway. Every day we postponed going to market was another day of lost earning potential...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you decided poisoning people was worth the risk?

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: Listen, it's not like it was good for business! But, all that talk about "Auguste" being harmful over time... Yelena was just speculating! The impact was practically negligible...

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: Unless you were particularly sensitive to elemental energy, or had an entire bottle shoved down your throat like Edgar, you could use the product for decades and be completely fine!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It may be true that there are no records of "Auguste" poisoning in Fontaine...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: But, even if no one was acutely poisoned... Willfully bringing a product to market despite explicit knowledge of its harmful effects is still a serious crime!

choices.text: The divine and noble "Auguste" originated from a Delusion...

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Hmph...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: That explains why you were so intent on keeping Yelena and Kirya's involvement a secret all this time, despite readily confessing to all your financial crimes...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: The Fatui, Delusions, "Auguste"... If the Marechaussee Phantom discovered the connection between the three, there would've been enough evidence to send you to the Fortress of Meropide for life.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Hah... If I'd known coming to Sumeru would put a target on my back, I would've been more than happy to stay there... At least that way, Lucien would still be alive...

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: All these years without any sign of Kirya, and he pops up out of nowhere the minute my brother and I get out of prison... It couldn't be any clearer who the kid's after!

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: "Auguste" was harmless before... The fact that it's killing people all of a sudden must be his doing as well...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: So, there's bad blood between you...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...What about Yelena's death? Was that a cover-up, too? A way to destroy evidence?

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: ...I'll admit, we thought about it at one point.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: We took care to disguise the products circulating on the market, and no one was questioning Yelena's fake identity...

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: But, if the Marechaussee Phantom decided to look into the flowerbeds, it would've been the end. Yelena's ties to the Fatui, the role of the Delusion... everything would've been exposed!

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Before we could even put our plan in motion... Yelena beat us to it. She burned all her flowerbeds... and threw herself into the fire as well.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: But... But if her goal was to destroy evidence, there would have been no reason to do that to herself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! She could've just burned the flowerbeds and fled with her brother...

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: ...I thought about it for a long time, but it wasn't until just now that I finally understood her reasoning.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Everything she did... it was for her brother, Kirya.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: One of the reasons they defected from the Fatui was the deterioration of Yelena's body due to her excessive use of a Delusion... She didn't want her brother to follow in her footsteps after her death.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: After arriving in Fontaine, Yelena continued using the Delusion to cultivate the "Auguste" flower, weakening her body even further. There were times when she couldn't even walk.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: ...So, she couldn't flee with her brother because she was afraid of holding him back...

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: ...If her true identity was exposed, she and her brother would face pressure from both Snezhnaya and Fontaine.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: The Auguste flower and Yelena's own corroded body both bore the mark of a Delusion. There would've been no way to avoid suspicion.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: So, in the end, she burnt it all to ash, including herself. With all the evidence erased, Kirya was free to take the Mora and run...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: So, the wealth you earned from "Auguste"... It wasn't destroyed in the fire. Yelena gave it to her brother?

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Most likely. Before Yelena died, she said if anything happened to her, she was going to leave everything to her brother... We just didn't realize she meant our cut as well!

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: That's why Lucien and I were searching for Kirya — to take back our Mora and the Auguste flower... We just didn't realize Kirya was baiting us the whole time... It was all a trap, haha...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, why is Kirya out for revenge, anyway? Doesn't he know about Yelena's decision to sacrifice herself?

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: ...I don't think he knew his sister was nearing death.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: Yelena always wore heavy makeup around him to conceal her deteriorating appearance. She kept herself busy with work to keep out of sight. That way, her brother wouldn't notice how she could barely walk...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then, all we need to do is tell Kirya what really happened, and then he'll give up on his revenge!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: ...I'm not so sure.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Even if he knew the truth, he'd still find someone to blame. He might think Yelena was forced into using a Delusion to cultivate Auguste... or something like that.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: It's hard to pull yourself out of that kind of hatred... especially when you've been living in that headspace for so many years.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: Very true... Even if Yelena's death was her own choice, I wouldn't call myself innocent either.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Edgar...! What are you talking about?

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: Think about it, Sylvain... If we hadn't been in such a hurry to capitalize on the "Perfume Mania" all those years ago, do you think Yelena would have elected to take those risks?

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: If we hadn't been so blinded by greed, so insistent on increasing the scale of the flower cultivation, do you think Yelena's health would have deteriorated as fast as it did?

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: If we hadn't invited the Marechaussee Phantom to our doorstep by breaking the law at every turn... Yelena could have survived...

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Hmph, she knew her limits. She knew her days were numbered! Maybe it was for her brother, but she was in it for the Mora just as much as us!

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: We were just trying to earn a bit of Mora... and, what, we deserve to die for that? Target me for being the mastermind, sure... But, what about Lucien? He was just following my orders!

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Lucien's crime... Was it really so extreme that he had to pay for it with his life?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...The only person that can answer that question is a judge.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Ha... Haha...

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: *sigh*... Fine. I've said my piece, anyway. Drag me back to Fontaine to stand trial, I don't care.

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: *sigh*... Three people from Fontaine, one from Snezhnaya, and a crime committed in Port Ormos... What a headache...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's going to happen?

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: ...Well, we can only wait until the Akademiya sends someone to deal with it. I'm guessing we'll have to contact Fontaine as well... In any case, we won't really know anything until tomorrow.

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: *sigh* With the exhibition, we don't even have space in Port Ormos to detain anyone... Such a headache...

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: Hmm... The hotel could suffice? You could station a few officers to keep an eye on Sylvain and myself.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: Although, with Sylvain's mental state and my physical one... I don't think you need to worry about a jail break.

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: Mr. Edgar, are you saying...?

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: ...If Sylvain is to stand trial, then I deserve the same fate. A crime is a crime, accomplice or not.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: I'd just like to take care of a few things before I go... say goodbye to my plants and all that.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: As for Sylvain... I'm sure he also has some goodbyes of his own.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: Would you be willing to grant that request, Sheriff?

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: Well... Alright. I'll talk to the Akademiya. No matter who you were in Fontaine, or what crimes you committed...

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: The man we grew to know in Sumeru proved himself to be a good person. Your request is granted.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: You have my thanks, Sheriff.

choices.text: But, if we wait until tomorrow...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Happen tonight...? Ah, you mean the possibility that Kirya might try to finish what he started?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! All we know is that he uses "Auguste" to poison people, but we still have no idea how to catch him in the act...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If he targets Sylvain or Edgar again, we might not be able to stop him!

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: That may be true, but what if we can take advantage of his desperation?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Desperation?

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: If we take advantage of this situation and lure him in on purpose... We might finally have the chance to talk to him.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Master, no! That's too dangerous...

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Ha... Haha... So, that's your plan.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: If Kirya learns we're being taken away tomorrow, his last chance to enact his revenge... would be tonight.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: In other words, you want to use us as bait to capture him!

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: ...Capture, not necessarily... I just want to talk. What, are you afraid of him?

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Afraid? Hah, this is my only chance to make him pay for what he did.

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: I'm spending the rest of my life in prison, anyway... I can't just sit back and let him ride off into the sunset with our fortune! There's no way I'm letting him get away with it, not after what he did to Lucien!

response.speaker: Sylvain
response.text: Hmph... As for the danger, everyone else just needs to make preparations in advance to protect us.

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: ...I'll admit, it could work. We'd just need to spread the word that Edgar and Sylvain are leaving tomorrow...

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: And then I'll station some of my men around the hotel... If we have your assistance as well, our chance of success would be even higher.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: I still have some reservations... But, if you insist on carrying out this plan, I won't deny you my help.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We can help stand guard.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I'll also keep watch.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: ...Although, I think Sylvain and myself should remain alone in our respective rooms.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: If Kirya noticed another person in the room, he might decide to turn back... And, besides, it's possible he's already transformed "Auguste" into a potent toxic gas.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh, you mean, if he doesn't see a way to get his hands on the two of you, he might get so desperate that he'll just start using "Auguste" on everybody?

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: If that were to happen, everyone standing guard... even the innocent citizens in Port Ormos, would all be in danger!

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: That's why everyone else needs to keep to the shadows... *coughing*

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: ...You're still recovering. You need to rest.

response.speaker: Edgar
response.text: *sigh* This old bag of bones doesn't bounce back like it used to... I suppose I'll just have to leave the rest to you.

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: Alright, we can figure out a plan to keep watch later. Right now, I say we split up and start spreading that information before it's too late.

choices.text: Doesn't that mean something could still happen tonight?
If the truth came out, the market for your product would be destroyed.

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: ...Have you heard? Mr. Edgar's been detained! He's being taken away tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: What!? He's the one who helped craft all the fragrances for our shop...

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: He taught my child how to make perfume... How could this happen...

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: ...He hasn't been convicted yet. Let's just wait and see what the court has to say...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everyone on the street is talking about the rumors... No matter where Kirya's hiding, he must've heard them by now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's head back to the hotel and take a break. We can see how the other preparations are going while we're at it!

talks.objective: Return to the area near the inn

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #Emilie! Sheriff Shyam wants to talk to you and {NICKNAME} about our plans for the night watch...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Thank you, Collei. But first... Here, I prepared a kind of herbal tea that helps calm the spirit. Why don't you have some?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, that's very kind of you, but I'm okay...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It's not good to be so tense, especially when we've got a long night ahead of us. I don't mean to put you on the spot, but I couldn't help but notice that something seems to be on your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Was... Was it that obvious?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: You seem very preoccupied with Kirya's "revenge"... If there's anything you want to talk about, I'm happy to listen.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... I...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Emilie, Collei... Oh, are we interrupting something?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: No, not at all. This will be easier to talk through with you here, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I've just been thinking... If Kirya has the capacity to commit murder while remaining completely undetected... Why didn't he target Sylvain along with Lucien last night?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: There was just a single door separating them. If his intention was to target both brothers, then there was barely anything standing in his way, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: When I accompanied Sylvain to his room after Lucien died, and saw how distraught he was... I suddenly realized...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Maybe Kirya did that on purpose. Maybe he wanted Sylvain to experience the pain of losing a loved one before he completed his ultimate revenge...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, did he attack Edgar as a warning, then? To scare Sylvain and Lucien?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Based on what we've heard about Kirya, that may very well be the case.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Losing his sister all those years ago... What has been going through his head? What has he been forced to endure?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Whenever I get to thinking like that, I just can't help but wonder... If I were in his place, would I be able to let go of that hatred?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Collei...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'm sorry. I know I shouldn't think like that, not after everything he's done... But, I just can't help it.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...There's nothing wrong with the way you're feeling. Empathy is a part of human nature.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: In all my years of cleaning up crime scenes, I've witnessed countless families mourn their loved ones. Their cries of devastation and anger still echo through my mind, even now.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Some of them even try to stop me, begging me not to erase the last remnants of their loved ones... But, getting swept up in those emotions will corrupt your judgment.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Surround yourself with fragrance for too long, and your sense of smell will become dull... Allow yourself to be consumed by your emotions, and you lose the ability to think rationally.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: So, while you hold onto that sense of empathy, you also need to ask yourself...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Do Sylvain and Lucien really deserve to die? How much did they truly know about the Fatui and the Delusion? Did they force Yelena to make those decisions?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Answering those questions requires a lot of time and evidence, while a single act of vengeance can put those answers forever out of our reach.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: I've witnessed a lot of deaths in Fontaine. When someone dies, a certain amount of information can be inferred from the traces left behind at the scene.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: But, generally speaking, death will just leave most questions unanswered, and the whole picture ever incomplete.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...Once you're consumed by hatred, it will become next to impossible to think about things that way. For someone like Kirya, I'm sure right and wrong lost all meaning a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: You're right. The fact that we can approach these questions from this perspective isn't because we're more rational than them... It's because we're fortunate enough not to have suffered that kind of loss.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: But, that also makes us perfectly positioned to stand on the outside... and try to pull them back from the brink before it's too late.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: I understand Kirya's decision, but I still want to stop him. Master, Sylvain, and Kirya... They all deserve to survive.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh, the fortunate... and the unfortunate...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: #Emilie! {NICKNAME}... Huh? Edgar, you're here too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two! Didn't you head back to your room to rest, Edgar? Is it really okay for you to be out and about like this?

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Aha... A little exercise never hurt anyone.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Besides, I don't have much time left in Sumeru, so I'd like to take care of my plants while I still can.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: We could do that for you, Master.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: No need. I've grown attached to these flowers, and this is my last chance to say goodbye... Come tomorrow, I'll be happy to entrust their care to you.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: ...I would imagine Sheriff Shyam is here for a more important reason?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah, that night watch! You mentioned earlier, we still need to confirm our plans...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: That's right. I've stationed some of my men around the surrounding area, but we still don't have anyone standing guard next to Sylvain's room.

choices.text: Next to Sylvain's room...

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: #Exactly. After some discussion, we concluded that Sylvain has the highest risk of being attacked next. You're the most skilled fighter here, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: And Emilie's expertise is sure to come in handy in a pinch... That's why I want you two stationed next to Sylvain's room. So, are you up for it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Fine with me. What about you, Emilie?

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: #Sounds perfectly reasonable. I'll be glad to have your help tonight, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: You mean, in Lucien's room?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You wait in Lucien's room for quite a long time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Not a peep! Has Kirya given up on his revenge?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just like that...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Guess we'll just have to keep at it!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The night deepens as the time passes...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still nothing unusual... Paimon took a peek into the room next door, and Sylvain's already sleeping!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shyam hasn't issued a warning either...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Perhaps Kirya's true motive was simply forcing Sylvain to confess his crimes?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: No, that can't be right... If all he wanted was for Sylvain to be convicted for his true crimes, he could have tipped off the Marechaussee Phantom years ago...

choices.text: And he already killed Lucien...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: There must be something we're missing... something extremely important...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe we just need to calm down a little... How about some tea? That herbal blend from earlier was pretty tasty...

choices.text: We can't abandon our post.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right... Um, maybe we can look for a different distraction, then? Like... Like looking at the flowers!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, there's a Glaze Lily here? Paimon didn't notice it earlier!

choices.text: Because they don't bloom during the day.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Flowers... Glaze Lilies... Incense...

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: Oh no... Sylvain's room! Quick!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what—

choices.text: Because they only bloom at night.
There's nothing here that we can use to make tea.
There's no reason to stop there.

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: Hey... Did you hear? Someone was attacked again last night!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: ...It was the older of the merchant brothers, right?

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: I think his name was Sylvain... Poor guy was murdered in cold blood!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: First it was Mr. Edgar, then that merchant named Lucien, and now this...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: ...Listen up, everyone. This is an active crime scene. Please, no loitering!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: ...It's been three days, and they haven't even caught a glimpse of the guy... What is going on...

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: Do you think it could be the work of an evil spirit?

dialogues.speaker: Crowd in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: I mean, how do you get away with something like that with so many people watching?

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Keep it moving, everyone... No loitering!

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: *coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: ...I suppose I'm next.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...You don't know that. Kirya already attacked you once, and you survived... Perhaps he doesn't consider your crime to be worthy of death...

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: You were the only reason I managed to survive, Emilie... Ah, I never did thank you for that, did I?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Even if I wasn't there, Tighnari was also in the vicinity. He would have been able to help.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Is that so...? I suppose I'm a very fortunate person, then...

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: I have exceptional students, caring friends, and the respect of my peers... If it is, indeed, my time to go, then I'll die without regrets.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: But, Kirya has nothing... Yelena is gone, and, now, his enemies are too.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: ...It really makes you wonder... if there's even a reason to keep on living.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: If you really want an answer, I suppose you'll have to ask Kirya himself once we finally catch him.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Ah, well, I hope it all goes well.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: ...Emilie, there's something else I'd like to ask of you... With everything that's happened, holding the exhibition is off the table now.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: But, so many flowers were transported here for the show, some of them thousands of miles away from their homeland... I can't let them wither away with no one to care for them.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Whether Kirya gets to me first, or I'm sent back to Fontaine to stand trial, I won't be around to look after them.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: I know it's a lot to ask... But, could I entrust them to your care?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Of course, Master.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Really...? I'm glad to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Now, I truly have nothing to worry about...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Sheriff Shyam still has some questions for me, so I've got to go.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Hah, go ahead. Best not to keep him waiting... He can be quite impatient.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry, Master.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: Ah... Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Emilie still isn't back... I hope she didn't run into any trouble...

choices.text: She's extremely meticulous...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Yeah, that's true...

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, I had my men start spreading the information you requested. The crowd is gone now, too... But, I have to admit, I'm not really sure what's going on...

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: After listening to Emilie's plan, I started getting the materials together and arranging personnel... I barely had a second to spare last night...

response.speaker: Shyam
response.text: To be honest, I'm still not sure how the crime was committed that night...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's pretty simple, actually...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The key clue was right in front of us the entire time!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Feel like you've been waiting to say that for a while...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, let's go! We'll show you where the culprit hid "Auguste"!

choices.text: I'm sure she's prepared to handle anything that might come her way.

dialogues.speaker: Flowers
dialogues.text: (The corners are filled with flowers from different nations. The fragrance is incredibly strong.)

dialogues.speaker: Flowers
dialogues.text: (The Glaze Lily is swaying gently, its petals closed. There's a ring of moisture around the rim of the petals that feels sticky to the touch.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is it!

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: But... Kirya was only in his teens back then. He wouldn't even be forty years old by now!

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Edgar's lived here for so many years. Even if he changed his appearance, going that long without giving anything away... It would be impossible!

dialogues.speaker: Innam
dialogues.text: ...B—Bad news, Sheriff! Mr. Edgar was attacked!

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Innam
dialogues.text: A dark, shadow-like figure just ran out of his room! It was giving off a really ominous aura...

dialogues.speaker: Innam
dialogues.text: But, before we could even react, the figure up and disappeared, like some sort of ghost or something... By the time we got a look inside the room, Mr. Edgar was gone!

dialogues.speaker: Innam
dialogues.text: Do you think Kirya kidnapped him?

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: I need you to think very carefully about this... Are you certain that figure wasn't Edgar himself?

dialogues.speaker: Innam
dialogues.text: Uh... I mean, Mr. Edgar was so frail... I don't see how he could've moved that fast...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: It would seem Master decided to tap into an ill-advised source of power.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: What? But, that's so dangerous with the condition he's in. It's...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Suicide.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: But why... Why would he do that? He has already accomplished his revenge!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: No... If his aim was to target "everyone" who had a hand in Yelena's death...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: If he left Sylvain alive yesterday, not out of a desire to see him suffer, but to confirm the truth about why Yelena chose to die...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Then, there's still one target left!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Sylvain and his brother seem wary of us... We should leave them be for now. We don't want to spook them.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You rush into the hallway and head for Lucien's room. You try to enter, but this door won't budge either...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: To tell you the truth, the exhibition has left us quite short-handed... We're lucky to have your help.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Sylvain still needs more time to calm down. We should finish investigating Lucien's room first...)

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: (This door leads to the hallway. The lock broke when we forced our way in.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This door was probably locked last night...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And the windows are shut tight too... Seems like the only way to get in would've been through Sylvain's room...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: My men and I will be stationed nearby to monitor the situation. A warning will be issued if any unusual activity is detected.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'll head into the mountains to keep an eye on everyone coming in and out of the area. Just leave the wilderness surveillance to the Forest Rangers.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I only have a basic idea of what happened, to be honest. I haven't really worked out the details...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Ah, so you're saying I'm the only one who's completely in the dark...

dialogues.speaker: Incense
dialogues.text: (The incense slowly rising into the air... It seems familiar somehow.)

dialogues.speaker: Incense
dialogues.text: (...Emilie checked last night. Turns out, it's Spirit Borneol.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wasn't this incense originally in Lucien's room? It must've been moved here before nightfall yesterday...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: ...The Glaze Lily? Huh, I think I've heard of it before. It's a flower from Liyue, right?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Well, did you know... it only blooms at night?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Emilie, you're back!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How did it go?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Exactly as expected.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: A flower that only blooms at night... Ah, like the Nilotpala Lotus!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: Exactly. Although, the Nilotpala Lotus wouldn't be a good substitute in this scenario. When it's closed, the gaps between the petals are too large.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: That's why "Kirya" chose the Glaze Lily as his mechanism... He would start by preparing an "Auguste" sample...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: That's right. He applied a diluted form of Slime Condensate to the petals to stick them together, and enclosed a sample of "Auguste" in the center.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: That way, the "Auguste" would remain trapped inside during the daytime, unable to seep between the petals and evaporate into the air. This also allowed the culprit to plant the poison well in advance while his targets remained oblivious.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: However... the diluted Slime Condensate wouldn't be viscous enough to prevent the petals of the Glaze Lily from opening at night. So, by nightfall, the flower would bloom, thereby forcing the target to inhale the "Auguste" trapped inside...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: And Kirya could execute his revenge without having to step foot inside the room during the night...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: By the next morning, the sample of "Auguste" would have nearly fully evaporated, the Glaze Lily would have already closed its petals, and any lingering odor would be concealed by the fragrance of the other flowers in the room.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...And his mission would be accomplished.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Wait a second... You're telling me this version of "Auguste" is so toxic, inhaling the minute amount trapped inside a flower is enough to kill a grown man?

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Then, how did Edgar even survive ingesting a whole bottle of the stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: That's because "Auguste" is just as dangerous now as it was all those years ago. The level of toxicity has never changed. Only a small subset of people are truly at risk.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Ah, you mean... people who are sensitive to elemental energy! So, it's just some sort of happy coincidence that Sylvain and Lucien are allergic to the stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: That can't be right... They were involved in the operation all those years ago... If the stuff gave them a bad reaction, they would've known from the very start!

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: I wouldn't use the word "allergic," necessarily. It's more like they're "susceptible" to its effects... But, that distinction isn't important right now.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: You can think of it this way: It's not that Sylvain and Lucien are innately sensitive to elemental energy, but that "Kirya" found a way to ensure that they would be...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Alchemically-produced essential oils, the Primordial Seawater that caused unrest in Fontaine not too long ago — all of those are substances that can heighten your sensitivity to elemental energy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And Kirya chose... Spirit Borneol.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That stuff gave us a lot of trouble when we first came to Sumeru...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. I definitely remember that.

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: In Sumeru, it's not uncommon to use incense indoors, so its presence wouldn't arouse suspicion. The flowers in the room could also serve to mask the scent...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Flowers were pretty important to his plan, huh... The Glaze Lily is native to Liyue. It would be completely unnatural to have one here in Sumeru if it weren't for the exhibition. What a coincidence...

dialogues.speaker: Emilie
dialogues.text: ...Actually, it's not a coincidence at all.

choices.text: The exhibition, the hotel...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder he was willing to pay a small fortune to rent out the hotel...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: He probably used the Mora Yelena left him, don't you think? That money was supposed to set him free...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: But, in the end... It was just a tool for his revenge.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: There's a saying among forensic doctors in Fontaine: "Every step you take leaves a mark."

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: But up until this point, we haven't been able to detect any trace of Kirya's activities. That's not because he was coming and going undetected, or because he's some kind of evil spirit.

response.speaker: Emilie
response.text: But because he's been disguised as someone else this entire time.

choices.text: It was all a meticulously designed trap.

dialogues.speaker: Edgar
dialogues.text: ...*coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: ...Shouldn't you be standing guard in the room next door? I would hate for Kirya to notice you here and abandon ship.

dialogues.speaker: Innam
dialogues.text: Phew... The crowd is finally gone...

dialogues.speaker: Oguz
dialogues.text: Can we even go forward with the exhibition...?

dialogues.speaker: Examine the body
dialogues.text: (The body has been cold for some time already... And there are no signs of a struggle. No further clues have been found yet.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it's been a day. Wonder if Tighnari discovered anything...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, things weren't looking good with Emilie's Master yesterday... We should check on things at the hotel first!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: There's no one here...?

dialogues.speaker: Sylvain
dialogues.text: ...Lucien! Lucien!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's Sylvain's voice! Hurry, let's check next door!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, looks like we've investigated as much as we can. Let's go report back to Emilie and Shyam!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn*... Another all-nighter... Paimon sure hopes Emilie's plan will go well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...But Collei still looks quite worried. Let's go talk to her!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If applied to the outside... You would still be able to smell "Auguste," even in the daytime...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If poured into the flower pot, the liquid would seep into the soil... That might prevent the substance from taking effect...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's a sticky substance on the edge of the flower petals. It's one I recognize...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If you stick the petals together with Slime Condensate, then, in the daytime, the Glaze Lily would act almost like a hidden container.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In Fontaine, I experienced how drinking Primordial Seawater made me more attuned to the element of Hydro... But, that substance would be hard to get around here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All kinds of essential oils commonly found in alchemical products can temporarily increase elemental affinity... But, it would be difficult to force someone to use them without knowing it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The incense I smelled earlier seemed familiar... Thinking back on it, I'm almost certain it was the scent of Spirit Borneol.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In Sumeru, scholars use Spirit Borneol to aid meditation and stimulate their connection to the Dendro Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Creating such an intricate mechanism out of a Glaze Lily... setting up the Spirit Borneol in advance... and arranging for Sylvain and Lucien to stay at the hotel...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...It all points to one person — the "expert" in charge of the entire exhibition.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Mora spent to rent out the hotel... the way the Auguste flower was cultivated... the "method" used to disguise his appearance...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...It all points to one person — the boy who inherited Yelena's legacy, her younger brother.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Kirya and Edgar... are one and the same.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound right... I need to think about this some more.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm... I can't seem piece this together in a way that makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The door gives way with bang, and you enter the room...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With another loud bang, the door gives way, and you enter the room...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With everyone's help, the news about "Auguste," as well as Edgar and Sylvain's impending departure, begins to spread...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Emilie rushes next door... A strange floral fragrance saturates the room.\nSylvain lies unmoving on the bed, already fully unconscious...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, in Sylvain's room...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We need to hurry. Now is not the time to wander.)
